That is independent confirmation, from a deck PowerPoint itself wrote, that an empty p:bldP is what a preset writes — which is why text.level/sequence 'asOneObject' cannot be recovered from it.

notMeasured.animation.timing.bounceEnd: the run that would have measured it wiped the deck's p:timing instead; see methodCaveats

methodCaveats: Saving costs the headless promise. File > Save is readable on the menubar surface but its refs cannot be pressed: the snapshot resolves the app as 'Microsoft PowerPoint' while the process owning the menubar reports 'PowerPoint', so a click returns STALE_REF on a source_process_identity mismatch, and --app PowerPoint is APP_NOT_FOUND. cmd+s is posted physically, so the window has to be focused first. Reading the pane stays headless; only the save does not.
A landed toggle is often reported as TIMEOUT (ax_error -25204) with postcondition_satisfied true, so the error has to be read rather than trusted.

Toggling Bounce End removed every p:timing element from the slide. The pane's Delete button sits beside these checkboxes, and refs on this pane were mis-resolving under memory pressure, so the likeliest cause is a ref landing on the wrong control rather than anything about Bounce End. The committed fixtures were unaffected — the damage was confined to the scratch deck — but it is why the remaining nine values are unmeasured: a surface that can mis-resolve onto Delete should be driven by gui_capture.py, which attributes every press to the effect it changed, not ad hoc.
